comment: I am writing to express my opposition to the request by the developers of Deer Valley Ski Area to form public improvement district/s for the development of their business property. I ask all of you to vote against approval. The redevelopment of Deer Valley Resort is for the benefit of an out-of-state corporation and private investors seeking the greatest amount of profit that can be extracted from their property through its association with the history and esthetics of our community. Our community is a place where the citizenry lives, but few derive their living. Park City is a daily commuter destination for thousands of people employed in tourist industries- our population triples in size every morning. The State of Utah has their fingers in our city and county operations and pushes our growth because they greedily desire the tax revenue that we generate for the rest of the state. Allowing DVC access to public bonds for their development will only allow them to overbuild their project. From groundbreaking it will draw additional day workers and ultimately droves of tourists that will further stretch the ability of our infrastructure and services to accommodate. Any purported benefits to our community offered by DVC such as their transit center or worker housing contributions are primarily to service their customers and benefit their own business. These “community benefits” will not offset the additional impact of this development project and will end up costing the taxpayers far more in the long run. The increased revenues from taxes that government entities are already counting will soon be absorbed to pay for the additional cost of supporting such a huge industry in our small town. The citizens of Park City do not need a larger resort, more tourists, more traffic, more commuters, more concerts and sporting events, additional traffic lights, higher prices, and crowding in our public facilities to enhance our quality of life. A PID is only requiring Parkites to pay for our own pain. Our town is already bursting at the seams from nearly year-round tourism and the cost of living in our town is onerous. Please vote against allowing the resorts to overbuild by subsidizing their profits through taxpayer investment.
source: eComment (written; published verbatim in council meeting minutes)

comment: I notice that once again, the "discussion" of a crossing near Snow Creek to Holiday Village Shopping Center is up for discussion. It seems like it's been discussed ad nauseam and because of that I submit my input in writing because I am not able to attend the meeting. The idea of a HAWK beacon is beyond absurd in terms of maintaining traffic flow as well as legitimate connectivity. We call ourselves a sustainable community. We provide free bus service, multi-use pathways, planned investments in transit lanes, park and rides, call ourselves a mountain town focused on recreation and the outdoors and we neglect to provide safe, efficient access of two critical neighborhoods. (Park Meadows and north PC to Bonanza and South PC) All this after our Planning Commission turned down an opportunity to do a private, public partnership with the Yarrow developers and help offset the costs. Those costs have tripled (or more) since a previous council approved it after a bond referendum successfully supported the connection. The waste and negligence regarding this topic is staggering. Please remember what this town is all about. Kicking this can down the road again is not the answer.
source: eComment (written; published verbatim in council meeting minutes)

comment: I am the Executive Director of Wasatch Immigration Project, as well as one of its volunteer attorneys.
